newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: NO OFFERS FOR COMMERCIAL BANK SALE - FINMIN.
newsitem.headline: NO OFFERS FOR COMMERCIAL BANK SALE - FINMIN.

text.p: The finance ministry said on Friday that it had for a second time received no offers to privatise the Lithuanian State Commercial Bank.
It was the second time the bank was offered for sale after no interested investors came forward the first time.
"We did not receive any proposals, not one," a spokesman for the finance ministry told Reuters. "The Lithuanian government must make a decision next week."
Thursday was the second deadline set by the finance ministry to receive proposals to privatise the troubled bank.
Analysts say State Commercial Bank more trouble than it is worth and that the other state-owned banks are more attractive.
The government had to inject 165 million litas of fresh share capital into State Commercial Bank last year after it teetered on the brink of crisis last summer.
The Bank of Agriculture is supposed to be next up for privatisation after State Commercial.
Officials have said the privatisation of Savings Bank depends on how the privatisations of the first two banks go.
